name: Wage at least the workplace minimum wage

references.title: UU 13/2003 art.88E(1)–(2) as amended by UU 6/2023; PP 36/2021 arts.23(1)–(3), 24(1), 25 as amended by PP 51/2023 and PP 49/2025 — the UMK of the worksite, else the UMP; art.23(2): where the wage is basic plus non-fixed allowances the basic alone must reach it (`terms.monthly_wage` holds only basic plus fixed allowances). Art.24(1): the minimum binds a worker with less than one year of service; longer service follows the wage structure and scale (art.24(2)). Micro and small enterprises are outside it (art.36). Daily and hourly wages are DAILY_MINIMUM_WAGE and HOURLY_MINIMUM_WAGE.

name: Overtime at most 4 hours a day

references.title: PP 35/2021 art.26(1)–(2): overtime at most 4 hours a day and 18 hours a week, not counting overtime on the weekly rest day or an official holiday. The hours worked are still paid (art.31), so the run warns rather than refuses.

rules.message: Overtime above 4 hours on a working day (PP 35/2021 art.26(1)); the hours are paid, the limit is breached.

name: Overtime at most 18 hours a week

references.title: PP 35/2021 art.26(1)–(2). The week is read as any seven consecutive days of the attendance window, which never misses a calendar week over the limit; rest-day and holiday overtime is outside the limit (art.26(2)).

rules.when: work.days.exists(d, sum(work.days.filter(x, (x.day_type == "WORK" || x.day_type == "") && x.holiday_kind == "" && calendar_distance_days(x.date, d.date) >= 0.0 && calendar_distance_days(x.date, d.date) <= 6.0).map(x, x.overtime_hours)) > 18.0)
rules.message: Overtime above 18 hours in seven consecutive days (PP 35/2021 art.26(1)); the hours are paid, the limit is breached.

name: Wage deductions at most 50% of the wage paid

references.title: PP 36/2021 arts.63–65: fines, damages, wage advances, rent, debts and their instalments, and recovered overpaid wages may together take at most 50% of each wage payment (art.65); contributions to the state and social security (BPJS, PPh 21) are outside it (art.64), and so is the pension offset against separation pay. Here: STAFF_LOAN, DEDUCTION and CLAWBACK_OVERTIME against the gross before the clawback. The UU 13/2003 art.62 damages a resigning PKWT worker owes (PKWT_EARLY_TERMINATION_BY_WORKER) are damages within the same 50%.

rules.message: Loan instalments, deductions, art.62 damages and recovered overpayments exceed 50% of this wage payment (PP 36/2021 art.65); the payslip is held.

name: Sector minimum wage not configured for the worksite

references.title: PP 36/2021 art.35D(1) (as amended by PP 49/2025 from 2026; with Permenaker 16/2024 art.7 for 2025); UU 13/2003 arts.88E(2) and 185: a governor’s sector minimum wage binds workers under one year of service in the sectors it names. Where the decree is known but its table was not read on an official copy (tracker ID-SETTINGS-15 lists the hosts tried), the run cannot floor the wage at it, so the payslip warns instead of silently flooring the worker at the UMK. Data: `rules.minimum_wage.unseeded_sector.areas.<code>` — `regions` (a province key covers its localities), `kbli` (prefixes of terms.facts.worksite_kbli; empty = any declared KBLI), `decree`; and `outside_tables` (version 1: every worksite area without a 2025 table in `by_sector`).
